issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares getTotalNumberOfStudents() as returning a String, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning an int. The template leaves a TODO for this method, and students are instructed to check the UML for the expected return type. This mismatch of return types is structural and will confuse students about whether to implement an int or String return type, possibly causing compilation or test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the return type across artifacts. Recommended: update the problem statement UML and any related text to declare getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int (and mention int in the instruction), so students implement and test an int return type. Alternatively, if String was intended, change the solution method to return String consistently and update examples/tests accordingly.
